rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition
primary_work: Merrill et al., Provable Limitations of Acquiring Meaning from Ungrounded Form, TACL 2021
decision: NARROWED BEYOND UNGROUNDED ASSERTION-BASED SEMANTIC EMULATION — NOT ADOPTED
reason: Assertion-like textual evidence can emulate an internal semantic-equivalence relation for strongly transparent languages, while context-sensitive language classes already admit formal ungrounded-emulation impossibility results. Neither boundary identifies an external latent intervention-target partition or a unique denotation. Even perfect recovery of language-internal equivalence and causal target blocks permits simultaneous cross-system permutation, and distinctions aliased in both the assertion and causal laws remain unidentifiable.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the finest raw-expression equivalence emulatable from all legitimate language-only assertions and dynamics and the finest intervention-target partition identifiable from all legitimate non-language observations and interventions, determine whether a preregistered interactive cross-system law uniquely identifies the residual equivalence classes and denotation, including context-opaque expressions, while eliminating every simultaneous utterance/target recoding preserving the complete language, causal, and interaction laws.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; theoretical primary work and no paper-specific official empirical implementation located
